subject: Request for log integrity confirmation — NeonPay incident
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@neonpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec@neonpay.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:14:23 -0700
Subject: Quick confirmation needed — potential NeonPay incident

Hi Aditya / Monica,

Heads up — our security team observed unusual requests to our NeonPay integration on 2027-06-24 around 22:10 UTC. We are investigating from our side; there’s no confirmed breach yet but compliance is asking for a formal check on Redwood’s side of the chain.

Specifically we need: (1) an affirmation whether Redwood observed any anomalous egress that could indicate data exfiltration, (2) a short summary of log integrity checks you performed, and (3) any artifacts you can share (redacted) to help our audit.

We appreciate a preliminary response today if possible. I’ve attached the NeonPay incident ticket export for context.

Attachments: neonpay_incident_export_20270624.json (ticket export)

—Jordan
Security Ops, NeonPay
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Security Team <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Incident Response <incident@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick confirmation needed — NeonPay incident

Team — forwarding NeonPay. They asked for an affirmation re: data exfiltration and artifacts. Please run the following checks and return findings/attachments: 

- Ingress/egress network logs for the period 2027-06-24 21:30 UTC to 2027-06-24 23:30 UTC (all edge routers servicing NeonPay tenant)
- Object store access logs (S3) for any NeonPay buckets and cross-account access events
- KMS/Key usage logs for any unusual decrypts or grant requests tied to NeonPay keys
- Serving runtime request IDs for requests from that timeframe (include request_id list and full request/response hashes where available)
- KV cache access patterns and any large snapshot exports or admin-initiated exports
- Host-level process and syslog scans for signs of exfil tooling or scheduled transfers

Please redact PII in attachments. NeonPay needs something they can present to their audit team — a concise summary plus the artifacts. If you need a forensic hold, let me know and I’ll coordinate legal.

Aditya Rao
Security & Partner Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Incident Response <incident@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 15:22:40 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Quick confirmation needed — NeonPay incident

Aditya — pulling together the initial artifacts. Preliminary results (short):

- Network egress: sampled flow logs for the time window show no outbound connections to rare/exfiltration-related endpoints. All external IPs map to known cloud providers and customer IP ranges.
- S3 access: no PutObject or GetObject patterns matching mass-downloads; several legitimate SDK multipart uploads observed tied to normal nightly jobs.
- KMS: normal decrypt counts; no abnormal or previously unseen principals used for NeonPay keys.
- Serving runtime: pulled request_ids 44d2f9a6.. and 51a8b2c1.. — response sizes are consistent with normal usage; no >1GB payloads.

I’m attaching a CSV with redacted request_ids and a short MD5 checksum list for the log files we exported. We’re continuing a deeper search (host forensic scans & cache scans). Expect a comprehensive summary by Monday.

Attachments: redwood_log_extract_20270625.csv

—Monica
Senior Incident Analyst, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 25, 2027 at 10:01 Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding NeonPay. They asked for an affirmation re: data exfiltration and artifacts...
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@neonpay.com>, sec@neonpay.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 13:50:12 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick confirmation needed — NeonPay incident

Aditya / Jordan / NeonPay team —

We’ve completed the scoped integrity and forensic checks for the requested timeframe (2027-06-24 21:30 UTC — 2027-06-24 23:30 UTC). Summary (formalized):

1) Data integrity checks performed
- CRC/MD5 checksums computed for all exported access logs (edge flow logs, application request logs, S3 access logs). Checksums match stored values in our immutable audit store.
- Log sequencing validated via monotonic sequence numbers; no gaps detected in the edge router logs that serve NeonPay traffic.

2) Access and egress findings
- No anomalous egress connections identified that would indicate mass data export. Egress destinations were to known cloud provider endpoints and NeonPay’s configured callback addresses.
- No background processes, scheduled transfers, or admin-initiated bulk exports targeting NeonPay data detected on the hosts serving the tenant.

3) KMS and key usage
- All KMS usage during the window aligns with tenant activity and service account principals. No unauthorized grant requests, and no asymmetric signing operations outside expected service accounts.

4) KV cache and snapshot checks
- No snapshot exports or admin snapshot downloads were recorded during or immediately before the window. Cache-hit patterns remained within historical baselines.

Conclusion (evidence-backed):
- Based on the scoped forensic checks described above, we found no evidence of customer data exfiltration or unauthorized export originating from Redwood infrastructure for NeonPay during the investigated timeframe.

Attached artifacts (redacted for PII):
- forensic_summary_neonpay_20270628.pdf (executive summary + verification steps + checksums)
- redwood_log_extract_20270625.csv (request_id samples, timestamps, response sizes)
- audit_chain_of_custody_20270628.txt (hashes and immutability stamps)

Notes & limits: the scope was limited to Redwood-managed infrastructure and the timeframe specified by NeonPay; if NeonPay’s internal systems were the source of the anomaly, that would be outside this scope. We recommend a joint call if you want us to expand the timeframe or add packet captures.

—Hannah Schmitt
Head, Security Investigations, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@neonpay.com>, sec@neonpay.com, ops@neonpay.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:43:10 -07:00
Subject: Formal attestation and artifacts — NeonPay scoped integrity check

Jordan / NeonPay team —

Thank you for the patience while we completed the scoped review. Please find a succinct attestation below and the attached artifacts for your audit. If you need a signed PDF for your records, please see signed_attestation_neonpay_20270628.pdf attached.

Formal attestation (scoped):
- Scope: Redwood-managed production infrastructure serving NeonPay only; timeframe: 2027-06-24 21:30 UTC — 2027-06-24 23:30 UTC.
- Findings: We executed network flow analysis, S3 access log review, KMS/key-usage audits, serving-runtime request sampling, KV cache snapshot checks, and host-level forensic scans.
- Attestation: Based on the evidence produced and the checks performed, Redwood Inference has found no evidence of unauthorized data export or exfiltration from Redwood-managed infrastructure impacting NeonPay within the scoped timeframe.

Attached: forensic_summary_neonpay_20270628.pdf, redwood_log_extract_20270625.csv, audit_chain_of_custody_20270628.txt, signed_attestation_neonpay_20270628.pdf

Next steps:
- If you want the scope widened (additional days, packet captures, or joint host-level triage), we can schedule a 30–60 minute call with our IR team this week.
- We’ll keep these artifacts on forensic hold per your request for 90 days unless you instruct otherwise.

If you need anything else or a tailored statement for your regulator, let me know and we’ll support.

Best regards,

Aditya Rao
Security & Partner Escalations
Redwood Inference
